AI, then edited by you · none here
You ask Bob for a cart helper. Nothing new to type.
UserPromptSubmit fires: a shell command, no model.
capture logs the session’s first prompt.
PostToolUse fires after every write_file, write_to_file, apply_diff, insert_content or search_and_replace.
capture keeps the exact lines and a file snapshot.
181 ms per capture, 0 Bobcoins. It never blocks Bob.
It labels each line: AI, AI then edited by you, or human.
Temporary-looking writes, like Bob’s earlier mock gateway, become items with a removal condition.
It attaches one JSON note to the commit.
Write lines are consumed; the prompt stays for later commits.
whyline report rebuilds the dashboard into a git-ignored file. git status stays clean.
You ask Bob why a line exists.
The skill runs whyline why on that line.
git blame finds commit d2b9320; why reads its note.
Bob wrote it in session a1c3e5f7, from this prompt. It is still a temporary item.
git blame tells you who. Whyline tells you why.
post-merge fetches the notes, then runs whyline check.
check recomputes every open item’s condition.
MockGateway has no references outside its file and tests, so the mock is now due.
The hook prints what is due. You decide: keep or remove.
Bob cannot shortcut it: the PreToolUse guard blocks any shell command that rewrites or deletes the notes.
Next session, SessionStart asks whyline what is due.
Bob’s context now says: the mock gateway is due.
You ask Bob to remove it.
The skill gathers evidence: check, git grep, a dry run.
Bob shows the evidence and waits. Nothing is deleted on its own.
Bob deletes it for real; the tests rerun: 2 passed.
Bob commits “remove L-12d3fa: until payments-v2 lands”. It never pushes.
post-commit records the removal in a new note.
